analysis.title: USA: Fed Governor Waller Says He Anticipates "Additional Hikes"
key_insights: Fed Governor Waller suggested he likely expects two additional rate hikes to be appropriate, which would raise the funds rate to 4.25-4.50%.
Waller said hikes do not need to come at consecutive meetings but should be in place in an acceptable period of time.
Waller said his view changed on a preponderance of evidence over several months that risks had shifted, reflecting a strengthened labor market and persistent inflationary forces.

Waller cited three forces undermining his faith that inflation is moving to 2%: no resolution to the Middle East conflict, signs the AI buildout is driving up high-tech consumer prices, and the risk of new tariffs.

Waller endorsed the Fed's current communication approach, including the SEP dot plot, as having the flavor of forward guidance without being forward guidance. His comment suggests he would likely oppose eliminating the SEP.
GS continues to expect one additional 25bp hike in December, which would raise the funds rate to 4-4.25%.
GS lowered its probability that the FOMC could pass on a December hike because Waller's speech is a hawkish shift from his earlier emphasis on the three-month annualized core PCE rate, now 2.0%.
GS expects that by March, the next meeting after December on an every-other-meeting schedule, inflation data will have improved enough to convince most of the FOMC that further hikes are unnecessary.
Waller's message is in line with comments last week from President Williams and Vice Chair Jefferson that pointed toward skipping a hike in October.
